topics.title: Factorisation by Taking Out Common Factors and Grouping Terms
topics.concept:
What is Factorisation?

Factorisation (or factoring) is the process of writing an algebraic expression as a product of two or more simpler expressions (factors). It is the reverse of multiplication.

What is Factorisation by Taking Out Common Factors?

When all terms in an expression share a common factor (number, variable, or both), we can "take it out" (factor it out) to simplify the expression.

Steps for Common Factor Method:

  1. Find the greatest common factor (GCF) of all terms
  2. Write the expression as: GCF × (remaining expression)
  3. Check by multiplying back

Example: 6x² + 9x

  • GCF of 6x² and 9x is 3x
  • 6x² + 9x = 3x(2x + 3)

What is Factorisation by Grouping Terms?

When there is no common factor in all terms, we can group terms that have common factors, then factor each group separately, and finally factor out the common binomial.

Steps for Grouping Method (for 4 terms):

  1. Group the terms into two pairs
  2. Factor out the common factor from each pair
  3. Look for a common binomial factor
  4. Factor out the common binomial

sections.content:
What is Factorisation? Factorisation (or factoring) is the process of writing an algebraic expression as a product of two or more simpler expressions (factors). It is the reverse of multiplication.

What is Factorisation by Taking Out Common Factors? When all terms in an expression share a common factor (number, variable, or both), we can "take it out" (factor it out) to simplify the expression.

Steps for Common Factor Method: 1. Find the greatest common factor (GCF) of all terms 2. Write the expression as: GCF × (remaining expression) 3. Check by multiplying back

Example: 6x² + 9x - GCF of 6x² and 9x is 3x - 6x² + 9x = 3x(2x + 3)

What is Factorisation by Grouping Terms? When there is no common factor in all terms, we can group terms that have common factors, then factor each group separately, and finally factor out the common binomial.

Steps for Grouping Method (for 4 terms): 1. Group the terms into two pairs 2. Factor out the common factor from each pair 3. Look for a common binomial factor 4. Factor out the common binomial

COMMON FACTOR METHOD - AREA MODEL:

    Expression: 6x² + 9x
    
    Area as rectangle:
    
        ┌─────────────┬─────┐
        │             │     │
        │    6x²      │ 9x  │
        │             │     │
        └─────────────┴─────┘
             2x         3
    
    Height = 3x
    Width = (2x + 3)
    
    Area = 3x(2x + 3)


FINDING THE GCF - STEP BY STEP:

    Terms: 12x³y², 18x²y³, 24x⁴y
    
    Step 1 - Coefficients: GCF of 12, 18, 24 = 6
    
    Step 2 - x terms: smallest power is x²
    
    Step 3 - y terms: smallest power is y¹
    
    GCF = 6x²y


GROUPING METHOD - VISUAL:

    Factor: ax + ay + bx + by
    
    Step 1: Group as (ax + ay) + (bx + by)
    
    Step 2: Factor each group:
           a(x + y) + b(x + y)
    
    Step 3: Common binomial (x + y)
           (x + y)(a + b)
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
    │                                     │
    │   ax + ay + bx + by                 │
    │         │                           │
    │    ┌────┴────┐                      │
    │    ▼         ▼                      │
    │  (ax+ay)  + (bx+by)                 │
    │    │           │                    │
    │    ▼           ▼

points: Factorisation = writing as product of factors
Grouping method: pair terms, factor each pair, find common binomial
Always check your answer by multiplying back
GCF includes both numerical and variable factors
Take out the smallest power of each common variable

topics.title: Factorisation of Trinomials and Difference of Squares
topics.concept:
What is Factorisation of Trinomials (Splitting the Middle Term)?

A trinomial of the form ax² + bx + c can be factored by splitting the middle term bx into two terms whose coefficients multiply to ac and add to b.

Steps for Splitting the Middle Term (when a = 1):

  1. Find two numbers whose product = c and sum = b
  2. Rewrite bx as the sum of these two numbers times x
  3. Factor by grouping

Example: x² + 7x + 12

  • Find numbers with product 12 and sum 7 → 3 and 4
  • x² + 3x + 4x + 12
  • x(x + 3) + 4(x + 3) = (x + 3)(x + 4)

What is Difference of Squares?

A difference of two squares is an expression of the form a² - b², which factors as:

\[

a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)

\]

Examples:

  • x² - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3)
  • 4x² - 25 = (2x - 5)(2x + 5)

Important Note: Sum of squares (a² + b²) cannot be factored using real numbers.

sections.content:
What is Factorisation of Trinomials (Splitting the Middle Term)? A trinomial of the form ax² + bx + c can be factored by splitting the middle term bx into two terms whose coefficients multiply to ac and add to b.

Steps for Splitting the Middle Term (when a = 1): 1. Find two numbers whose product = c and sum = b 2. Rewrite bx as the sum of these two numbers times x 3. Factor by grouping

Example: x² + 7x + 12 - Find numbers with product 12 and sum 7 → 3 and 4 - x² + 3x + 4x + 12 - x(x + 3) + 4(x + 3) = (x + 3)(x + 4)

What is Difference of Squares? A difference of two squares is an expression of the form a² - b², which factors as: \[ a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b) \]

Examples: - x² - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3) - 4x² - 25 = (2x - 5)(2x + 5)

Important Note: Sum of squares (a² + b²) cannot be factored using real numbers.

SPLITTING THE MIDDLE TERM - VISUAL:

    Factor: x² + 7x + 12
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │                                         │
    │  x² + 7x + 12                          │
    │         │                              │
    │         ▼                              │
    │  Find two numbers:                     │
    │  Product = 12, Sum = 7 → 3 and 4      │
    │         │                              │
    │         ▼                              │
    │  x² + 3x + 4x + 12                    │
    │         │                              │
    │         ▼                              │
    │  x(x+3) + 4(x+3)                      │
    │         │                              │
    │         ▼                              │
    │  (x+3)(x+4)                           │
    │                                         │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────┘


FACTORING WHEN a ≠ 1 (ax² + bx + c):

    Factor: 6x² + 13x + 6
    
    Step 1: Find product = a×c = 6×6 = 36
    Step 2: Find two numbers whose product = 36 and sum = 13
            Numbers: 9 and 4 (9×4=36, 9+4=13)
    Step 3: Split: 6x² + 9x + 4x + 6
    Step 4: Group: (6x²+9x) +

points: For x² + bx + c: find factors of c that sum to b
For ax² + bx + c: find factors of ac that sum to b, then split and group
Difference of squares: a² - b² = (a - b)(a + b)
Sum of squares a² + b² cannot be factored with real numbers
Always check if further factorisation is possible
Verify by expanding the factored form

topics.title: Sum and Difference of Cubes
topics.concept:
What are Sum and Difference of Cubes?

Expressions of the form a³ + b³ (sum of cubes) and a³ - b³ (difference of cubes) can be factorised using special formulas.

Sum of Cubes Formula:

\[

a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2)

\]

Difference of Cubes Formula:

\[

a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)

\]

How to Remember the Formulas:

FormulaSigns in Factors
a³ - b³(a - b)(a² + ab + b²)

Memory Trick (SOAP):

Same sign, Opposite sign, Always Positive

  • For a³ + b³: (a + b)(a² - ab + b²)
  • For a³ - b³: (a - b)(a² + ab + b²)

a³ - b³(a - b)(a² + ab + b²)

SUM OF CUBES - GEOMETRIC VISUAL:

    a³ + b³ represents volume of a cube side a plus cube side b
    
        ┌─────┐
       /│     /│
      / │    / │
     └──┼───┘  │
     │  └───┼──┘
     │ /    │ /
     │/     │/
     └─────┘
    
    This can be rearranged into:
    (a + b)(a² - ab + b²)


DIFFERENCE OF CUBES - FORMULA BREAKDOWN:

    a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + ab + b²)
    
    Expand to check:
    (a - b)(a² + ab + b²)
    = a(a² + ab + b²) - b(a² + ab + b²)
    = a³ + a²b + ab² - a²b - ab² - b³
    = a³ - b³ ✓


SOAP - MEMORY AID:

    Sum of Cubes:  a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²)
                             ↑       ↑     ↑
                             S       O     P
    
    Difference:    a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + ab + b²)
                             ↑       ↑     ↑
                             S       O     P


EXAMPLES WITH NUMBERS:

    8x³ + 27 = (2x)³ + (3)³
    
    a = 2x, b = 3
    
    = (2x + 3)[(2x)² - (2x)(3) + 3²]
    = (2x + 3)(4x² - 6x + 9)
    
    
    64x³ - 125y³ = (4x)³ - (5y)³
    
    a = 4x, b = 5y
    
    = (4x - 5y)[(4x)² + (4x)(5y) + (5y)²]
    = (4x - 5y)(16x² + 20xy + 25y²)

points: Sum of cubes: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²)
Difference of cubes: a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + ab + b²)
SOAP rule helps remember signs: Same, Opposite, Always Positive
The quadratic factor (a² ∓ ab + b²) cannot be factored further with real numbers
Always check if terms are perfect cubes first
Apply formulas only when both terms are perfect cubes
